title: add `draw --version` reading the version dynamically from pyproject
body:
draw-cli currently has NO `--version` flag — it is the only tool in the ecosystem missing it. `pyproject.toml` declares `0.1.0` but `bin/draw` prints no version anywhere.

## What
Add `draw --version` (and `-V`) that prints `draw <version>`, reading the version DYNAMICALLY (single source of truth = pyproject), matching the bump-version-on-release pattern (agent-tools#99; same as rig#71 / task#23 / 3d#10).

## How
- `importlib.metadata.version("draw-cli")` when installed as a dist.
- Fallback to parsing `pyproject.toml` `[project] version` with a stdlib-scoped regex (NO `tomllib` — `requires-python = ">=3.9"`, tomllib is 3.11+).
- Do NOT hardcode the literal version string.

## Acceptance
- `draw --version` prints the pyproject version.
- A drift-guard test pins the printed version == pyproject `[project] version` so it cannot drift.
- ruff clean; version bumped on this feature ship (0.1.0 -> 0.2.0).

title: `draw --version` prints "unknown" when run via the installed symlink
body:
PR #6 added `draw --version`, but it prints `draw unknown` for the REAL installed invocation.

## Root cause
`draw` is on PATH as a symlink: `/Users/ultra/.files/bin/draw -> .../draw-cli/bin/draw`. `_version_from_pyproject()` derives the pyproject path from `__file__`, which under a symlinked invocation is the SYMLINK path (`~/.files/bin/draw`), so `dirname(dirname(__file__))` points at `~/.files` — no `pyproject.toml` there → returns `"unknown"`.

This is the `single-file-live-symlink-cli` pattern: the tool is run through a symlink to a checked-out repo. The metadata path also misses because draw-cli is not pip-installed as a dist.

## Repro
```
$ draw --version
draw unknown        # expected: draw 0.2.0
```

## Fix
Resolve the symlink before deriving the repo root: `os.path.realpath(__file__)`. Add a regression test that invokes draw THROUGH a symlink (the path the existing tests skip) and asserts the real version.

## Why it slipped CI
Tests + CI invoke `bin/draw` by its real path, never via a symlink, so the fallback path that breaks in production was never exercised through a link.

title: Deferred review findings from pipx packaging (PR #9)
body:
Deferred review findings from the pipx-packaging work (PR #9). None are
release-blocking; tracked here so they aren't silently dropped. Several of the
security items are about the **shared install-skill machinery**, which is common
across the `review` / `tg` / `draw` CLIs (cross-CLI), not draw-specific — fixing
them in one place ideally covers all three.

## Security (shared install-skill machinery — cross-CLI: review / tg / draw)

- **`.env` comment stripping can truncate a token containing `#`.** `cli.py`
  `_load_env()` strips everything after `#` from a value (intended: inline `.env`
  comments). HF tokens today don't contain `#`, so they're unaffected — but a token
  that *did* contain `#` would be silently truncated with no warning. Consider only
  treating `#` as a comment when preceded by whitespace, or documenting the limitation.
- **`.env` permissions are never checked.** A world-readable
  `~/.config/draw-cli/.env` would leak `HF_TOKEN`. Warn on lax mode (e.g. group/other
  read bits set) and document `chmod 600 ~/.config/draw-cli/.env`.
- **install-skill blurb mechanism is a prompt-injection surface.** The installed
  SessionStart hook `cat`s `~/.agents/skills/.blurbs/*.md` into every session's
  context. That directory is shared across `review` / `tg` / `draw`; anything that
  can write a `.md` there can inject instructions into all agent sessions. Consider an
  allowlist of known blurb files and/or content hashes.
- **`install_agent_skill(name)` doesn't validate `name` for path traversal.** Safe
  today (the only caller hardcodes `"draw"`), but `name` flows into
  `~/.agents/skills/<name>` / `.blurbs/<name>.md` path construction. If this ever takes
  external input, a `name` like `../../...` would escape. Validate/whitelist the name.

## Minor / cleanup (draw-cli)

- Lazy stdlib-only imports (`re`, `shutil`, `json`, `pathlib`) inside the install-skill
  helpers could move to module top — they're stdlib, so no lazy-heavy-import benefit;
  they're scattered for locality only.
- `cli.py`'s `ImportError` message hardcodes the GitHub URL
  (`git+https://github.com/alex-mextner/draw-cli`) while `install.sh` parameterizes it
  via `GITHUB_USER` / `REPO`. Drift risk if the repo ever moves; consider a single source.
- `bin/draw` has no `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard (it `raise SystemExit(main())`
  at module top). Harmless for a shim, but inconsistent with the package modules.
- Duplicated `sys.path` bootstrap across `tests/test_smoke.py` and `tests/test_version.py`
  → could move to a `tests/conftest.py`.
- No full test coverage for the harness-mutating install-skill code
  (`_ensure_sessionstart_hook`, `_append_marked`, `install_agent_skill`) — it edits
  `~/.claude/settings.json` and writes skill files; worth a tmp-home test.

## install.sh (optional cleanup deferred from PR #9)

- `install.sh` calls `command -v "$TOOL"` twice; could collapse into a single variable.
  Left untouched in PR #9 (not obviously safe to refactor blind).

title: chore: add scripts/deploy.sh so rig apply keeps this tool fresh
body:
## What
Add scripts/deploy.sh (safe fast-forward git pull of the live checkout). Reference implementation: tg-cli's scripts/deploy.sh at /Users/ultra/.files/repos/tg-cli/scripts/deploy.sh — refuse on dirty worktree, detached HEAD, or diverged branch; exit 0 on both up-to-date and successfully deployed.

## Why (motivation)
rig-cli 0.8.0 (PR https://github.com/alex-mextner/rig-cli/pull/106) runs a tool's scripts/deploy.sh on every rig apply to keep the live checkout fresh; tg-cli has one, this repo does not, so it silently drifts stale

## User impact
the user keeps running a stale installed CLI: new features and fixes already exist on origin/main but the user never sees them until they remember to manually pull the checkout

## Cost of inaction
stale-tool drift continues for every tool except tg

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] scripts/deploy.sh exists, does a safe fast-forward git pull of the checkout (refuse on dirty/detached/diverged), exit 0 on up-to-date/deployed
- [ ] rig apply output shows [deploy.sh: ok] for this tool

(none)

title: Disable leftover SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW via committed .ship-config
body:
## What
gh ship refuses draw-cli PRs that have zero GitHub reviews. The durable off-switch is a committed repo-root .ship-config with SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0 on the PR base branch. origin/main currently has no .ship-config: git show origin/main:.ship-config returns fatal path does not exist. Env SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0 is ignored after https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/624.

## Why (motivation)
Same leftover gate as the other CLIs. Documented config, not env: committed SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0. Precedent: https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/commit/17431bf446dffd76016cf84704773a91806e93ba and merged https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/pull/451. Durable key from https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/600 and https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/609.

## User impact
If you try to land a draw-cli change with gh ship, the merge stops even when GitHub itself does not require an approving review. You sit waiting for an external review the repo already decided it does not want as a merge gate. Tiny chores cannot ship until someone posts a GitHub review. After the key is on origin/main, later PRs can ship without that extra forced review.

## Cost of inaction
Every future draw-cli gh ship of a zero-review PR keeps failing. Agents and humans burn time posting dummy reviews or cannot merge at all. The intended SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0 policy never takes effect because the env form is ignored.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Repo-root .ship-config exists on the feature branch and contains exactly SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0 followed by a newline. Proof: git show of that file on the branch. — forced: one-line repo config and GitHub PR files tab; no rendered UI surface
- [x] A PR against main adds only that file, with a chore(ship) commit that Refs this ticket and does not use Closes, Fixes, or Resolves. Proof: the PR files tab shows only .ship-config. — forced: one-line repo config and GitHub PR files tab; no rendered UI surface

- Merge commit: https://github.com/alex-mextner/draw-cli/commit/c3adfb2c5c6edad57952821b47550c7d6bd5ac72

## Skipped gates

title: chore(rig): enable worktree-only guard for the primary checkout
body:
## What
Enroll agent_hooks.worktree_only: true in rig.yaml so the primary draw-cli checkout is guarded against direct edits, forcing all work through rig worktree create per the documented AGENTS.md worktree lifecycle.

## Why (motivation)
Historically many stray sibling worktree dirs accumulated across the rig ecosystem because nothing enforced the worktree convention at the repo level.

## User impact
Agents/CI attempting to edit the primary draw-cli checkout directly are blocked, keeping it clean and preventing future stray worktrees.

## Cost of inaction
Stray worktrees keep accumulating and the primary checkout drifts dirty.
